discussion.body:
Don't really have anywhere to credit these sources in docs until I find something
For now I want to keep links to a few sites that've really helped with research

nodes.body: > TODO: various forums from building docs timeline

Was searching to figure out is Daikatana was ever made Open-Source
They got a Linux port, like most 90's Quake-based games

## Findings:
 * [DaikatanaNews.net](http://www.daikatananews.net/)
   * [OpenKatana](https://www.moddb.com/games/decay-tempus/news/openkatana-news-update), last updated: 2013
     * [OldTimes Software](https://oldtimes-software.com/): OpenKatana Devs
       * [The Data Dungeon](https://thedatadungeon.com/): Pre-release Archive (demos etc.)
 * [Daikatana Restoration Project](https://github.com/atsb/daikatana-restoration-project/)
   Like [Daikatana 1.3](https://bitbucket.org/daikatana13/daikatana/), but less Closed-Source

> Nested because one site led to the next

nodes.body:
The Data Dungeon has a lot of interesting stuff:
 * Dark Messiah of Might & Magic demo & sdk
 * Vampire the Masquerade: Bloodlines community patch & sdk
 
 Some pages even have internet archive references!
 No links to the ModDB & PlanetVampire archives of the above sdks tho

The devs are also on GitHub: [TalonBrave.info](https://github.com/TalonBraveInfo)
As are [OldTimes Software](https://github.com/OldTimes-Software)

[DKRP](https://github.com/atsb/daikatana-restoration-project) includes [qfiles.h](https://github.com/atsb/daikatana-restoration-project/blob/main/user/qfiles.h)

There's even some references to what changes each increment of `BSP_VERSION` added

Found this while looking into the `GINSU.INI` in Quake 3 (Dreamcast) `.cdi` files
[The history of Sega Smash Pack Dreamcast](https://www.sega-dreamcast-info-games-preservation.com/en/sega-smash-pack-dreamcast-history-prototype-iso-gdi)
